configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and four fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.

configs.description: The 7050CX3-32S with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-500AC-F supplies and FAN-7000H-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7050CX3-32S-F.

gaps.note: Guide Table 4 prints 206 W typical and 314 W maximum for the 7050CX3-32S; the data sheet prints 168W / 343W for the same measure (typical at 25 C, 50 percent load, excluding transceivers; the guide gives no conditions). The guide's are modelled, as the newer of the two documents for what it prints.

gaps.note: Guide Table 1 gives 8.8 kg (19.4 lbs) and the data sheet 20 lbs (9.1 kg). The guide's is in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet). The guide's is in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

The 7050CX3-32S is mapped to D-1 by its four fans (data sheet), its two supplies and its front management ports. The data sheet's "Rear View" photograph (PDF page 3) shows the same shape but is a thumbnail.

gaps.note: The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-14 are isometric drawings with no measure and the kit guides for KIT-7001, KIT-7101 and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.

gaps.note: Figure C-13 is too small to resolve any per-port lamp, so none is modelled and the port lamp states of guide Appendix A.1.2 are not attached to a port.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 40.6 cm (19 x 1.75 x 16 inches), 8.8 kg (19.4 lbs). Data sheet: 44 x 4.4 x 40.64 cm, 20 lbs (9.1 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 44 cm (440.0 here). The height is 43.7, as the library's other 7050 devices. The depth is the guide's 40.6 cm (406.0); the data sheet's 40.64 is the same figure to one more place. The weight is the guide's 8.8 kg; the data sheet's 9.1 kg is in the gap `weight`. 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the median of the grey pixels (neither black nor white, low saturation) of the guide's figure C-13, #7a7b7b. The figure is a raster and its lighting is not known, so the shade is estimated.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7050CX3-32S-F and -R ("front-to-rear air, 2xAC" and "rear-to-front air, 2xAC"), the "#" SKU ("configurable fans and psu") and the -D SKUs with expanded memory and an SSD. Only the front-to-rear build is a configuration: the -R build seats PWR-500AC-R and FAN-7000H-R, which are not modelled (gap `airflow-reverse`). The "#" SKU is an order of parts, not a part number a DCIM can hold. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-500-DC-F supply is a spare, so the DC configuration is an example with no part number. The -D builds differ in memory and storage, which a configuration cannot state.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings that carry no measure, and the kit guides are not held. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: storage -40 to 70 C. The storage temperature differs: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The figure prints the maker's wordmark and the model line at the top left. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The blue outline round each group of four cages and the tiny legends over them are not drawn.

front-ports.note: Figure C-13 at 1.293 px/mm. Thirty-two QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows (ports 1 to 32), sixteen columns in eight groups of two, the tab centres of ports 1, 3, 5, ... 31 reading 41.0, 59.6, 87.1, ... mm across: a 18.6 mm step inside a group (the registry's ganged-QSFP pitch is 19.0, which is used) and a 46.1 mm step between groups, so a 8.1 mm gap between the groups of two. The rows read at 14.2 and 31.2 mm down (cage centres), a row pitch of 17.0; the perforated band the figure draws between them is not drawn, because the numerals are set there. Two SFP+ cages (33 over 34) at the left, centred 15.2 mm across on the same rows. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) and the data sheet ("1+1 hot-swappable power supplies and four N+1 hot-swap fans"): THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE FOUR FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-13 passes. The raster is 575 x 174 pixels; the body between its plate edges measures 569 px wide and 56 px tall (aspect 10.2) against the data sheet's 440 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 1.293 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor). One pixel is 0.77 mm, so every position is good to about 1 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The cage columns were read from the white port-number tabs in a three-times enlargement.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-1 is a 576 x 155 px raster whose chassis is 573 px between its edges (1.302 px/mm over the 440 mm body); positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7050CX3-32S is mapped to D-1 by its four fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two supplies and its management ports at the front (Figure C-13 draws them there, and D-1 is the rear for "models with management ports in the front"). The data sheet (PDF page 3) captions a rear photograph for the 7050CX3-32S, a supply, four fan modules and a supply, which agrees; the guide does not name the figure, so THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet34 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched the held documents (the guide and the data sheet) for an end-of-sale or end-of-life notice for the 7050CX3-32S: none. No web search was made, so this is a statement about those documents only.

management-block.note: Figure C-13 callouts 1, 6 and 7 draw a stack at the right, 399.6 to 417.7 mm across and 4 to 38 mm down: the Ethernet management port (top), the USB port and the console serial port (bottom), the order of the callouts. The plate and cutouts are those of arista/7280tr3-40c6, moved to the measured x.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The guide's Table 5 says "Attach ground directly to back" for this model (Figures 4-1 and 4-2, the earth grounding pad on the rear); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2 gives the port lamp states of the family. Figure C-13 draws a strip of tiny lamps under each group of four cages at the bottom edge that Figure C-13 does not call out and that cannot be counted at 1.3 px/mm. No port lamp is modelled (gap `port-lamps`).

port-numbering.note: Figure C-13 (callout 8, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on across the sixteen columns, 1 to 32, and 33 over 34 at the left. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over its cage; a seated cage hides what is painted under it, so the numerals are set in the band between the two rows, the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 206 W / 314 W for the 7050CX3-32S with PWR-500AC or PWR-500-DC. The data sheet prints 168W / 343W, typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports, excludes transceivers". The guide's are modelled and the data sheet's are in the gap `power`; the two are the same measure, so this is a conflict. The guide does not state the conditions of its figures.

rear.note: Figure D-1 at 1.302 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right. Each supply reads 86.5 mm wide (the PWR-500AC is wider than the PWR-511's 73.5 mm) at 4.8 and 344.5 mm across and 1.85 mm down, an inlet at the left and a fan guard with a red diagonal handle at the right. Four fan modules at a pitch of 59.4 mm, the grilles starting at 108.8, 168.9, 228.1 and 287.0 mm across (each module a honeycomb grille, a red handle and a label tab, 56.4 mm wide, so the modules stand 3 mm apart), at 2.55 mm down. A narrow plate of symbols beside the last fan and a blue plate beside the first, which the figure draws, are not drawn.

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7000H-F/R" and the spares FAN-7000H-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7000H-R (rear-to-front). Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The four fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7000H-F; the -R module is not modelled.

sources.note: 7050 Series 1RU (Gen 3) Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-00141-08, 57 pages, copyright 2025, PDF created 2025-08-19 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7050_1RU_Gen3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), section 4.1 and Table 5 (grounding), Appendix C (Figure C-13, the front panel of the DCS-7050CX3-32S), Appendix D (Figure D-1, the rear panel with management ports in the front), Appendix E (field replacement). 7050X3 Series 10/25/40/50/100G Data Center Switches Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0040-46 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7050X3-Datasheet.pdf): the model comparison, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; a `find` of the intake folder for 3D files found none) and a Visio stencil master that was not used. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

status-lamps.note: Figure C-13 callouts 2 to 5: a system status lamp, a fan status lamp and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies, four lamps in a column at the right of the management block with a legend beside each. They sit 419.0 mm across and 7.0, 10.1, 13.2 and 16.3 mm down; the order (system, fan, PS1, PS2) is the callout order of the figure.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated band along the top, 0.8 to 5.3 mm down, from 27 mm across to the management block. It is drawn in its measured extent, not hole by hole.
